name: The demo data shows every part of the console except the new triage panel
description:
`pnpm db:seed:demo` is the documented way to look at the console without waiting for a real pull request, and it covers the inbox, every verdict, a claim, the history and the dynamic results. After the cross-round work it has a blind spot in exactly the place with the most new behaviour: **the carried-over triage panel is empty, so it does not render at all.**

That is not a cosmetic gap. The panel is hidden entirely when there is nothing to show — no empty state, no hint that the screen exists — so somebody looking at a freshly seeded console cannot tell the feature is there. Seeing it today means writing the rows by hand in SQL, which is both slow and a good way to invent a state the real pipeline never produces.

**Done when:** seeding the demo data produces a pull request whose triage panel is populated and worth looking at — a finding still open, one whose thread has been closed, one proposed as fixed with the evidence behind that proposal, and one the reviewer took back. Along with them: a finding with no thread at all, where confirming it closed is the only thing on offer, and one on a repository where we may not close conversations, so the panel's explanation of that limit is visible rather than theoretical.

The seed keeps the guarantees the rest of it already has: it refuses to run against production and it can be run twice without making a mess.

**Not part of this.** The two release switches stay where they ship — off, and dry run on. Faking either in demo data would teach a rollout order that is not the real one; the seed should say what to run and flip instead, so the screen can be seen in the state an operator will actually meet first.

Found while building CZ3TDR1-664. Next task in the chain, on top of it.
